newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trichet sure of final deal on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Trichet sure of final deal on stability pact.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said he had "no doubt" European countries would iron out their differences and agree a stability pact to enforce fiscal discipline under monetary union.
Trichet, speaking to Germany's Die Zeit weekly in a report published on Wednesday, also said there was no need to alter the exchange rate between the French franc and the German mark.
Trichet sure of final deal on stability pact

Trichet said hard bargaining over Germany's call for a tough stability pact with automatic penalties for countries which violate the Maastricht treaty after monetary union was a matter "of definition."

"We are all support, in certain cases, fines against budget sinners for the stability of the euro. We just have to decide when sanctions should apply automatically and when a political judgement is needed," he said in remarks published in German.
"I haven't the slightest doubt that the partner countries will eventually reach an agreement," he told Die Zeit.
Trichet rejected calls for a franc devaluation from French eurosceptics, saying that 80 percent of his country's economic problems were structural, not cyclical.
"We are highly competitive, we have a balance of payments surplus, our inflation is among the lowest and all factors for a strong inflation-free recovery are in place," he said.
"We are at least as attached to our franc as the Germans are to their mark."
Trichet is due to hold a speaking engagement in Bonn on Thursday evening and will speak on "Unity and Stability in Europe, a French Central Bank Perspective."
